first.rationale: Two of three current problems (activation down 6%, onboarding down 4%) map directly onto prior durable findings (memory_31, memory_86) that simplifying/shortening onboarding lifts activation and completion — a single lever addressing two symptoms at once, which is efficient given only one experiment slot. The competitor pricing pressure (favoring memory_73's promotional pricing) is tempting but risky: matching aggressive entry pricing could win price-sensitive, lower-LTV SMB accounts at the cost of margin and long-term qualified revenue quality, which conflicts with the stated objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. I'm verifying the two onboarding-related memories before committing since they're doing double duty as justification and I want confirmation they generalize to current conditions (competitive pressure wasn't present when those experiments ran). Promotional pricing and enterprise sales-assist remain plausible alternatives worth reconsidering next cycle, and referral/activation-messaging address different funnel stages not currently the acute bottleneck.
